decisive_items: hypodense mass containing areas of calcification
mass appeared to nearly obliterate the lumens of the main and hilar pulmonary arteries
without attachment to the pulmonary valve
response.rationale: The calcified intraluminal mass nearly obliterating main and hilar pulmonary arteries without valve attachment is characteristic of pulmonary artery sarcoma, whereas chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension typically shows organized thrombus with less discrete mass and more chronic history; D-dimer elevation is nonspecific.

rejected.why: Pulmonary embolism usually lacks calcification and valve-sparing mass; D-dimer elevation is nonspecific.
Tricuspid regurgitation is a secondary finding, not the primary cause of the pulmonary artery mass.
Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma does not produce a calcified mass obliterating pulmonary arteries.
Aneurysm would show dilation without an intraluminal calcified mass.
Fibrosing mediastinitis typically causes extrinsic compression, not an intraluminal mass with calcification.
